before: for i:=0; i<4; i++ initializes once, tests before each body and updates after each completed body.
continue proceeds to the next iteration; the update still runs before the next test.
break stops this nearest loop instead of skipping only one pass.

Optional local transfer task: Trace initialization,condition,body,and update for both versions. You may trace it without a Go compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: The loop starts i at 0, checks `i < 4`, runs its body, then adds 1 with `i++`. It repeats that check before each new turn.
`continue` skips the rest of the current turn. In this loop, i++ still runs before the next check.
`break` leaves this loop completely. It does not move to another turn.
This loop stops because i increases until the check is false. When writing a loop, check how it will reach its stopping point.
The screen shows `0`, `2`, and `3` on separate lines. continue skips the display instruction when i is 1.
Replace continue with break in the same example. Now reaching 1 ends the loop.
